subject: history
topicDisplay: HL Regional Option: History of the Americas
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The United States declared independence from Britain in:
questions.explain: The Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.

questions.q: Simon Bolivar led independence struggles in:
questions.explain: Bolivar helped liberate several South American territories from Spanish rule.

questions.q: The American Civil War (1861-65) was fought over issues including:
options: Slavery and the preservation of the Union
questions.explain: Disputes over slavery and states' rights led the Southern states to secede.

questions.q: Abraham Lincoln's 1863 proclamation that declared enslaved people in Confederate states free was the:
questions.explain: The Emancipation Proclamation (1863) declared freedom for enslaved people in rebel states.

questions.q: The 13th Amendment (1865) to the US Constitution abolished:
questions.explain: The 13th Amendment abolished slavery throughout the United States.

questions.q: The Monroe Doctrine (1823) warned European powers against:
options: Further colonisation or intervention in the Americas
questions.explain: The Monroe Doctrine opposed European interference in the Western Hemisphere.

questions.q: 'Manifest destiny' was used to justify US:
questions.explain: Manifest destiny held that the US was destined to expand across the continent.

questions.q: The Great Depression began with the 1929:
questions.explain: The 1929 stock-market crash triggered the Great Depression.

questions.q: Franklin D. Roosevelt's response to the Great Depression was the:
questions.explain: The New Deal provided relief, recovery and reform in the 1930s USA.

questions.q: The Cuban Revolution of 1959 brought to power:
questions.explain: Castro's revolution overthrew Batista and established a communist state in Cuba.

questions.q: The US civil rights movement of the 1950s-60s sought:
options: An end to racial segregation and discrimination
questions.explain: The movement campaigned for equal rights and the end of segregation.

questions.q: The Mexican Revolution began in:
questions.explain: The Mexican Revolution began in 1910 against the Diaz regime.

questions.q: The Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) brought conflict between the USA and the USSR over:
questions.explain: The crisis was a Cold War nuclear standoff over missiles in Cuba.

questions.q: The 'Great Migration' involved African Americans moving from:
options: The rural South to northern cities
questions.explain: The Great Migration saw millions move north seeking work and escaping segregation.

questions.q: The Spanish-American War (1898) resulted in the US gaining control of territories such as:
questions.explain: The 1898 war expanded US influence, gaining former Spanish territories.

questions.q: Martin Luther King Jr. led the civil rights movement using:
questions.explain: King championed non-violent direct action to achieve civil rights reforms.

questions.q: The New Deal is often summarised as providing:
questions.explain: The 'three Rs' capture the New Deal's aims during the Depression.

questions.q: A comparison of US and Latin American independence movements would consider:
questions.explain: Comparing cases across the Americas is a core Paper 3 skill.

questions.q: Assessing the causes of the American Civil War involves weighing:
questions.explain: Multiple interacting causes (slavery, economy, states' rights) explain the war.

questions.q: The abolition of slavery in the United States followed the:
questions.explain: Slavery was abolished (13th Amendment) at the end of the Civil War in 1865.

specSource: IB Diploma History guide (first assessment 2020); HL regional depth options (Paper 3): History of the Americas
